about: Earth's Extremes on the Outdoors page (tools/site/build_pages.py extremes_list). art names an engraving drawn by the build; source is where the figures come from; mine, where there is one, links to my own photographs of the place.

extremes.name: K2
extremes.text: The second-highest mountain on Earth and the hardest of the 8,000-metre peaks: first climbed in 1954, and not in winter until January 2021.

extremes.name: Alpamayo
extremes.text: A near-perfect pyramid of fluted ice, its southwest face ribbed from summit to snowfield. A 1966 poll of climbers named it the most beautiful mountain in the world.

extremes.name: Chopicalqui
extremes.text: A broad, heavily glaciated giant beside Huascarán, Peru’s highest peak, climbed by its southwest ridge through séracs and crevasses since 1932.

extremes.name: The Amazon
extremes.text: The largest tropical rainforest on Earth, home to about one in ten known species. Its trees breathe out so much water that they help make their own rain.

extremes.name: Atacama
extremes.sub: of rain a year in places
extremes.text: The driest non-polar desert on Earth. Some of its weather stations have never recorded rain, and its soils are close enough to Mars’s that rover teams test there.

extremes.name: Bryce Canyon
extremes.text: The largest collection of hoodoos on Earth: limestone spires split apart by ice that freezes and thaws in their cracks on more than 200 days a year.

extremes.name: Angel Falls
extremes.text: The tallest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth, dropping 807 m in a single fall off the edge of Auyán-tepui, a table mountain rising out of the rainforest.

extremes.name: Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa
extremes.text: Measured from its base on the ocean floor, Mauna Kea is taller than Everest. Its neighbour Mauna Loa is the largest active volcano on Earth.

extremes.name: Kelp and black coral
extremes.sub: of giant kelp in a day
extremes.text: Giant kelp grows up to 60 cm a day into forests over 45 m tall. Far below, deep-sea black corals off Hawaiʻi have been dated to more than 4,000 years old.

extremes.name: Hang Sơn Đoòng
extremes.text: Found by a local man, Hồ Khanh, in 1990 and first explored in 2009: more than 5 km long and 200 m high, with its own jungle under collapsed skylights, and its own clouds.

extremes.name: Challenger Deep
extremes.text: The deepest known point in the ocean: Everest would fit inside with more than 2 km of water to spare. Far fewer people have been to the bottom than to space.

extremes.name: Vostok Station
extremes.text: The coldest air ever measured at a weather station, on an ice sheet more than 3.7 km thick. Satellites have since found hollows of the plateau near −98 °C.
